findings.description: The three hunks attributed to `.claude/adapters/cheval.py` are YAML (`backward_compat_aliases:`, `agents:`, `tier_groups:`) and clearly belong to `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml`. Meanwhile the actual cheval.py change the report describes for fd8aaae3 (the `--help` text now saying 'other providers min(16000, catalog max_output_tokens)') is absent from the diff, even though new test c124-1.4-3b asserts on exactly that string. The hunk offsets (+40 lines before line 1173) also show the new `claude-opus-5-5` / `claude-sonnet-5` catalog entries and the `aliases.opus` / `aliases.cheap` retargets were omitted. If cheval.py genuinely embeds a YAML copy of the catalog, that is a second source of truth that the yq-reading tests would not see.
findings.failure_mode: Reviewers cannot verify the change that c124-1.4-3b depends on, nor the catalog entries that every other updated test depends on; a stale help string or missing entry would only surface as a test failure after merge.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-submit the diff with the correct path for the YAML hunks and include the cheval.py / base.py help-text and comment changes plus the omitted catalog hunks (claude-opus-5-5 entry, claude-sonnet-5 entry, aliases.opus, aliases.cheap).

findings.description: `deep-thinker` is rebound from the GA `gemini-2.5-pro` to the alias `gemini-3.1-pro` (backed by `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`) while keeping `requires: thinking_traces: required`. The neighbouring `gemini-3-flash` comment explicitly documents a `fallback_chain` to `gemini-2.5-flash` so `_resolve_active_model` can demote on UNAVAILABLE; the new deep-thinker comment asserts thinking_traces but says nothing about a fallback. No test in the diff dry-runs `--agent deep-thinker`, and the E2E table lists no deep-thinker evidence.
findings.failure_mode: If the preview entry's capabilities do not declare thinking_traces, or if its probe state goes UNAVAILABLE with no fallback_chain, every `cheval --agent deep-thinker` call hard-fails at resolve time instead of demoting to gemini-2.5-pro as it did before this change.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` carries `thinking_traces: true` and a `fallback_chain: [gemini-2.5-pro]`; add a bats case that runs `cheval --dry-run --agent deep-thinker` and asserts the resolved model and that `requires` is satisfied.

findings.description: The hunk adds bare self-maps for `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-opus-5.5`, citing the rule that 'BB and advisor tier_aliases pass the bare id'. The report says `cheap` now resolves to `claude-sonnet-5`, which per the cycle-124 header comment was not part of that generation's self-maps. No `claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-sonnet-5.5` self-map is added in this hunk, and the visible context lines show none.
findings.failure_mode: If `claude-sonnet-5` lacks a bare self-map, any BB or advisor path that passes the bare id (the exact case the comment describes) fails to resolve the new `cheap` tier, while the dotted `claude-sonnet-5.5` form that users will type by analogy with `claude-opus-5.5` is also unresolvable.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify `backward_compat_aliases` contains `"claude-sonnet-5": "anthropic:claude-sonnet-5"` (and the dotted form if a 5.x exists); add a `c124-1.3-2`-style self-map test and a generated-maps grep for it, mirroring what c124-1.3-3 does for opus.

findings.description: Two suites gain a hard runtime dependency on a `yq` CLI (c124-1.4-1 and `_expected_max_output` in gen-bb-registry-codegen.bats) with no `command -v yq || skip` guard and no declared dependency. Two mutually incompatible `yq` implementations exist (mikefarah Go yq v4 and kislyuk python-yq); older mikefarah releases reject `-r`. The rest of this test tree already reads the catalog through `$PYTHON_BIN`. Separately, c124-1.4-1 now derives its expected value from `aliases.opus` in the same file cheval reads, so it no longer pins `opus → claude-opus-5-5` in this suite; the report's 'none was weakened' claim relies on c124-1.3-1 and gen-adapter-maps for that pin.
findings.failure_mode: On a CI or contributor host without `yq` (or with an old mikefarah build), five tests fail with an unrelated 'command not found' / 'unknown shorthand flag' error, masking real regressions in the effort-flag and BB codegen suites.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the catalog with `$PYTHON_BIN -c 'import yaml,sys; ...'` as the schema suite does, or add `command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"` in setup(); keep at least one literal `claude-opus-5-5` assertion in c124-1.4-1 so the test retains regression value.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/model-config-v3-schema.bats:V3 (c126): every beta-header value the schema accepts, the adapter accepts (never looser)
findings.description: The cross-check reaches into the private `anthropic_adapter._BETA_HEADER_RE` and applies `.match()` (prefix-anchored) rather than calling the adapter's actual validation entry point. If production validates with `.fullmatch()` or applies additional checks (length, allowlist membership), the test can print OK for a value such as `a-2025-01-01-` that the schema accepts and runtime rejects, which is precisely the gap the test exists to close. The test also assumes the schema stores the pattern at a hard-coded JSON path.
findings.failure_mode: A schema-valid `params.beta_headers` entry passes `validate_v3` and this guard, then cheval refuses the model at load with a beta-header error; the test silently stops guarding when the adapter renames or relocates the regex.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose and call the adapter's public validator (e.g. `is_valid_beta_header()` or whatever `_apply_beta_headers` actually uses) instead of `_BETA_HEADER_RE.match`, and assert the schema path exists with a clear message before indexing into it.

findings.description: The generated-maps assertion adds `["claude-opus-5-5"]="anthropic"` (provider map) but not the `MODEL_IDS` self-map `["claude-opus-5-5"]="claude-opus-5-5"`, unlike the paired checks it sits next to for `claude-opus-5`. The report states BB and advisor tier_aliases pass bare ids through `MODEL_IDS`.
findings.failure_mode: A generator regression that emits the provider row but drops the MODEL_IDS self-map for the new id passes this test while bash callers passing the bare `claude-opus-5-5` fail to resolve.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `grep -q '\["claude-opus-5-5"\]="claude-opus-5-5"' "$GENERATED_MAPS"` alongside the provider check, and the same pair for `claude-sonnet-5`.
